title: Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Prior-Term Lookback and Effective Date of Overlap Cancellations
content:
**Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — overlap schedule for certificates ending on confirmed borrower coverage.**

**Prior term.** The prior term is the term whose expiration date is the current term's start date (the current term being the term on the certificate's latest renewal entry, or on its issue entry when it has no renewal entry). Its premium and start date are those on the issue or renewal entry of that term.

**Lookback.** When the certificate has a prior term and the borrower's coverage start falls on or before that prior term's start date, the whole premium of the prior term is added to the overlap credit; when it falls after the prior term's start date and before its expiration date, the prior term's premium multiplied by the days from the borrower's coverage start to the prior term's expiration date, divided by the days in the prior term and rounded half to even to the cent, is added to the overlap credit; in every other case nothing is added.

| Certificate has a prior term? | Borrower's coverage start | Added to the overlap credit |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | On or before the prior term's start date | Whole prior-term premium |
| Yes | After the prior term's start and before its expiration | Prior-term premium pro rata by days to the prior term's expiration |
| Yes | On or after the prior term's expiration (the current term's start) | Nothing |
| No | Any | Nothing |

**Effective date and booking.** The earliest term the credit reaches is the prior term when the borrower's coverage start falls before the current term's start date and the certificate has a prior term, and the current term otherwise. The cancellation takes effect on the borrower's coverage start or, when that start falls before the start date of the earliest term the credit reaches, on that term's start date; the credit is booked as a flat cancellation when the cancellation takes effect on the start date of the earliest term the credit reaches and as a pro rata cancellation otherwise.

Days between two dates are counted from the earlier date to the later date, the earlier date excluded and the later date included.

*Hypothetical case.* A certificate renewed once: prior term 5 April to 5 April, current term from that date. A borrower policy effective 20 May of the prior term reaches back into the prior term; the cancellation takes effect on 20 May and is booked as a pro rata cancellation. Had the borrower policy taken effect on 1 April, before the prior term began, the cancellation would take effect on the prior term's start date, 5 April, as a flat cancellation.
